newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sees Q1 above $0.18/shr estimate.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sees Q1 above $0.18/shr estimate.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Thursday it expects its fiscal first-quarter earnings per share for the period ended March 31 will be above the Wall Street analysts' consensus estimate of $0.18 and at least equal to last year's $0.22.

Last year's $0.22 excludes a one-time gain on the sale of the company's Italian foods business. The 1997 first quarter outlook excludes a one-time loss of about $8.40 a share from the anticipated sale of Snapple this year, the company said in a statement.

The better-than-expected results are being driven by volume growth across Quaker's name-brand and bagged ready-to-eat cereals, double-digit volume growth in U.S. Gatorade and volume growth in hot cereals, Quaker said.
"Our core food businesses and Gatorade continue to deliver strong operating results and value," said William Smithburg, Quaker chairman, president and chief executive officer.

"Year-on-year comparisons show that volume growth in these businesses is outpacing category growth and enabling Quaker to more than offset significant challenges presented in the last 12 months," he said in a statement.

He said the challenges included a 15 percent average price decrease across brand-name ready-to-eat cereals, the absence of earnings from Quaker's frozen foods business which was divested in July 1996, spending on first-quarter Diet Snapple initiatives, and significantly increased spending behind the U.S. Foods business.
Ready-to-eat cereal volume growth of over 25 percent highlights the strength of both Quaker's name-brand cereals (Cap'n Crunch and Life) and its line of Quaker value-priced bagged cereals, he said.

U.S. Gatorade volume growth of 15 percent in the first quarter was attributed to the launch of the new Frost line and category growth. For the 12-week period ended March 15, Gatorade thirst quencher garnered an 84 percent share of the U.S. sports beverage segment, Smithburg said.
The first quarter also showed volume growth for European Foods and Latin American Gatorade, he said.
Quaker will report full results for the first quarter on April 23.
On March 27, Quaker announced its intent to sell Snapple Beverages to Triarc Companies Inc for $300 million. The transaction is expected to close about 60 days from the date of the announcement.
